ai.description: The Red Sand Boa reaches 60–90 cm. It is uniform reddish-brown to tan. It features a blunt, shovel-like head and a thick, cylindrical body ending in a truncated, rounded tail.
ai.identificationRemarks: The Red Sand Boa is best distinguished by its blunt, cylindrical tail that closely mimics the shape of its head, a feature unique among similar Indian sand boas.
ai.habitat: The Red Sand Boa inhabits arid and semi-arid regions, including sandy deserts, scrublands, and dry deciduous forests, typically at elevations below 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: When threatened, the Red Sand Boa often curls into a tight ball and raises its blunt, rounded tail to mimic its head, confusing predators about which end to strike.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Eryx johnii* is ovoviviparous, typically breeding from winter to spring. Females give birth to a litter of 6–14 live young after a gestation period of several months.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Eryx johnii* is widely distributed across the Indian subcontinent, primarily inhabiting arid and semi-arid plains from sea level up to 1,500 meters elevation.
